clue.text: Flipping keen singer

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it end to end, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: keen and avid both mean eager

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a very enthusiastic vocalist, with 'flipping' as a mild British curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive intensifying 'keen', but it signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: Disrespect North American tribe? Time to be prudent

parts.note: to dis is slang for to disrespect
the Cree are a First Nations people of Canada and the northern US
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone has insulted a tribe and is being told it is time to act sensibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being discreet means being careful and circumspect, close in sense to wise caution.

clue.text: Five help to get piano in flat

parts.note: V is five in Roman numerals

indicators.note: something that gets another thing inside it takes it in, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: aid is help
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Five people help move a piano into an apartment, a flat being a British word for one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a home to carry the piano into, but it is the definition: lacking liveliness. V plus AID, with P put inside the help.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapid means dull and insipid, the same sense as flat for a performance or drink lacking sparkle.

clue.text: Stop by a blue house

parts.note: a bung is a stopper
taken as written
blue and low both mean depressed

explanation.surface: An instruction to call in at a house painted blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a single-storey dwelling, a type of home.

clue.text: Excited by romantic meeting, daughter's getting changed

parts.note: worked up, keyed up: excited
a date is a romantic appointment
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter, thrilled about a date, is getting dressed for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changed' suggests changing clothes for the date; here it means revised.
explanation.definitionFit: Something updated has been revised to the latest version, that is, altered.

clue.text: Growing frustrated with cipher? This should prevent people in the way getting hit

definitions.text: This should prevent people in the way getting hit

parts.note: green describes growing plants and foliage
cross means annoyed
a cipher is a code

explanation.surface: Someone grows annoyed with a cipher they cannot crack.
explanation.walkthrough: The Green Cross Code is the British road-safety routine taught to children for crossing the street; 'in the way' means in the roadway.
explanation.definitionFit: This rule set teaches pedestrians to cross roads safely, so its purpose is to stop them being struck by traffic.

clue.text: Ending with ale drunk, becoming dull

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and jumbled, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A night that ends with too much beer and gets dreary.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden means heavy and sluggish, so leadening is turning lifeless and dull.

clue.text: Broad's poor delivery?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in cricket, a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach, penalised with a run

explanation.surface: A dig at a bad ball from Stuart Broad, the England fast bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuart Broad was a famous England cricket bowler, so the possessive invites reading him in; in cricket a wide is a delivery too far from the batter to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide is a synonym of broad, and in cricket it names an illegal ball bowled beyond reach.

clue.text: Fear of being shut in front of cockpit with a BA pilot — hours wasted

indicators.note: wasted suggests ruined or wrecked, so the letters lose their order
the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of cockpit
taken as written
taken as written; BA is British Airways
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An airline pilot stuck for hours in the cockpit develops a fear of confined spaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Claustrophobia is the irrational dread of enclosed or confined places.

clue.text: Silk slip wrapped around one? Ecstasy!

indicators.note: a thing wrapped around another encloses it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to slip is to fall
I is the Roman numeral one
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A silk slip dress wrapped around someone, met with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silk slip' reads as one garment, but silk is the definition and slip the wordplay. FALL goes around I, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: Faille is a soft ribbed fabric traditionally woven from silk.

clue.text: Market forces stallholder initially to change plan and dump dye

indicators.note: initially points to the very first letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the opening letter of stallholder

indicators.note: changing the words means rearranging their letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A market trader decides to change tactics and get rid of some dye stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Supply and demand are the economic pressures that set prices in a free economy.

clue.text: One's in the main embarrassed by '80s haircut

parts.note: going red with embarrassment
the mullet, short at the front and long at the back, was a 1980s hairstyle

explanation.surface: Someone mainly embarrassed by a hairstyle from the 1980s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'mostly', but the main is the sea; the answer is a fish that lives there.
explanation.definitionFit: The red mullet is an edible sea fish, so it is one creature found in the ocean, poetically called the main.

clue.text: Want nag to throw off the Parisian

indicators.note: throwing something off discards it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: to needle someone is to nag or provoke them
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A wish for a horse that will unseat a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' suggests an old horse throwing its rider, but it is the verb, to pester. NEEDLE loses LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something can mean to require it, as in 'the garden wants weeding'.

clue.text: Call hospital department — it has cut leg

indicators.note: something cut has been shortened, so its final letter is lopped off

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Phone the hospital ward: it has a patient with a gashed leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut leg' reads as an injury for the department to treat, but cut means losing the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle a work is to give it a name, which is what calling something means.

clue.text: Cryptic end in sight? Rush and use a reference book

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so the letters appear in a disguised order
the end in a word is its closing letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the closing letter of sight
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crossword solver, the end in sight, is urged to hurry and consult a word book.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'Cryptic' is a puzzle the solver nearly has; here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a book of synonyms consulted for words, a classic reference work.

clue.text: Read about beginnings of internet lawlessness? Go off line

indicators.note: about suggests being turned round and moved around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: beginnings are the first letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the opening letters of internet and lawlessness

explanation.surface: Reading about online crime, then logging off the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off line' sounds like going offline from the internet; it means a train leaving the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: To derail is to leave the track, as a train does when it comes off the railway line.

clue.text: Small bit of hair on head regularly shed — very worried

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a tress is a lock of hair

indicators.note: shedding at regular intervals drops every other letter, keeping the rest

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of head

explanation.surface: Someone shedding hair from their scalp, losing it from worry.
explanation.walkthrough: Stress makes hair fall out, which the surface plays on. In a down clue, 'on' places the first part above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed means under strain, anxious and tense, close to extremely anxious.

clue.text: Recover from op — cure's radical

indicators.note: radical suggests a drastic overhaul, so the letters are thoroughly reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Convalescing after an operation whose treatment was drastic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'recover' as getting well; it means getting back money or losses.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to regain or get back what was lost, such as costs.

clue.text: Bird urine disgusting by the sound of it

indicators.note: judging by the sound means the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: pee is a colloquial word for urine
foul means revolting

explanation.surface: A complaint that bird droppings are revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: Peafowl is the species name covering peacocks and peahens, large pheasant-family birds.

clue.text: Ken succeeds in understanding

indicators.note: to succeed is to come after, so the first piece goes behind the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
ken is range of sight or knowledge, as in 'beyond our ken'

explanation.surface: A man named Ken does well at grasping things.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken looks like a man's name; it is the old noun for range of vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep, intuitive grasp of something, which is a form of comprehension.

clue.text: Secret that is about new heads of state in Denmark

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer piece goes around the rest

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: heads are the leading letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the opening letters of state, in and Denmark

explanation.surface: A confidential report on new rulers in Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside information is confidential, known only to insiders, so the adjective means private.

clue.text: King remains hasty

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A monarch is still impetuous.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash decision is one made impetuously, without careful thought.

clue.text: Partner in fracas — so CIA testifies

indicators.note: in tells you the letters are sitting inside the following run of words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of fracas, all of so and CIA, and the start of testifies

explanation.surface: An accomplice caught in a brawl, so the CIA gives evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: An associate is a colleague or business ally, someone you work alongside.

clue.text: Place in which you'll see termination of Roman?

definitions.text: Place in which you'll see termination of Roman?

indicators.note: something seen within a place is held inside it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: an area is a place or region

indicators.note: a termination is an ending, so the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of Roman

explanation.surface: Where you would have watched a Roman being put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: gladiators and Christians met their end in the Roman amphitheatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena was the amphitheatre floor where Romans watched combat and executions to the death.

clue.text: Hands up for trade

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: paws is jokey slang for hands

explanation.surface: A show of hands to vote on a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands up' reads as a stick-up or a vote, but up is the turnaround signal in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another, the basis of barter.

clue.text: Passion slowed Doberman's barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, including the s

explanation.surface: A dog's fervour is dampened by its own noise.
explanation.walkthrough: With a Doberman around, 'barking' reads as the dog's noise; it is British slang for crazy, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being warm-blooded figuratively means ardent and hot-tempered, so the noun names fervour.

clue.text: OK to go with expert

parts.note: to pass is to go by
able means skilled

explanation.surface: Permission to set off accompanied by a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Passable means adequate or acceptable, just good enough, which is what OK means.

clue.text: Give worker a round of applause

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pass something over
second meaning: a labourer, as in farmhand
third meaning: as in 'give her a big one'

explanation.surface: An instruction to clap for a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings, not two: verb, labourer and ovation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to pass over, a manual labourer, and an ovation in 'a big hand'.
